statements.status_notes: The sort utility's begfield() function in GNU Coreutils is vulnerable to a heap buffer under-read that may allow access to memory outside the allocated buffer when a crafted command uses the traditional key format with an out-of-range character position, due to unsafe pointer arithmetic causing integer wraparound.
statements.impact_statement: GNU coreutils' sort utility has a heap buffer under-read reachable only via the traditional key-specification syntax (+POS1[.C1][OPTS]) with an out-of-range character position. The container's build steps and runtime entrypoint use only rm, ln, mkdir, chown, chmod, wget, tar, unzip, and sha256sum — a source review found no invocation of sort anywhere in this repository's Docker build or runtime path. This OS package's version is not pinned by this repository — it tracks whatever the unversioned eclipse-temurin:21-jre-noble base image tag resolves to at build time. Confirmed by pulling the current base image directly and checking installed package versions (not from repo-pinned config), it ships coreutils 9.4-3ubuntu6.3, the fixed release, as additional defense-in-depth.
